A second place in the A long jump (Adrian Phillips) backed by a win in the B (Richard Danso) was followed by good points in the A 100 where we saw the welcome return of Darren Chin (who lost last season through injury) backed up in the B 100 by Phillips Idowu (honing his speed).

And the sprints that followed continued the momentum with Wade Bennett Jackson making a welcome season’s debut after injury, claiming a fine 3rd in the A 100m followed by a second placing in the B race for Darren Chin.

Big headwinds made sprinting difficult and with strong fields and five false starts Darren Chin struggled in the A 100 but the situation was immediately recovered when Wade Bennett Jackson won the B race.
Only 4/100ths covered the first four and it was James just out of the ‘medal’ positions. In the B race Darren Chin started badly and got up well to finish second.

Darren Chin also suffered at the hands of the local club as youngster Rion Pierre ran an extraordinary 10.39 with the wind speed being variously reported as 0.0 and 1.2mps; in truth there was no wind reading at all but it was probably around 3.0mps.

Now back to the track where the 100m was disappointing, with Darren Chin’s blocks slipping and Jason Hussain looking as though he had just got out of bed.

Darren Chin timed the next handover to perfection and Wade Bennett Jackson entered the home straight with a clear lead. Easing over the last ten metres and looking left he was almost run down by the fast finishing Russian, Yepishin, who was on his right and had earlier finished third in the 100 to Wade’s fifth placing.
Darren Chin was also in good form with sharp times in the 100m and 200m, and there seems to be no stopping Joe Ive who took maximum points in the pole vault with 5.30m.
With top point scorers William Sharman and Darren Chin on their way to the World Student Games and Joe Ive injured, we cast the net wide to chase every point.

Belgrave’s Darren Chin ran the third leg and will be disappointed that silverware evaded the team in this event. Also competing on day one was William Sharman who cruised through his heat securing third spot for a place in the semi’s.

On match day this had fallen to just James Ellington as Darren Chin had pulled an abductor doing Friday evening start practice. But worse still was to come; James had a trapped sciatic nerve which reduced his stride length.
